messages.content: Good morning. This is Madam Wong Kah Yee, tariff analytics lead at MyxTel commercial. We have a CFO review on Friday and I need to investigate why prepaid ARPU on tariff plan `tp-pp-rd-3day-99` dropped 14% week-on-week. Can you start by listing all the tariff metrics that track ARPU-related KPIs?
Good morning, Madam Wong. Certainly — I will pull the catalogue of ARPU-related tariff metrics now.

messages.name: list_tariff_metrics
messages.content: {"error": {"http_status": 429, "code": "rate_limited", "message": "Too many list_tariff_metrics calls from tenant tnt-myxtel-comm in last 60s (limit: 30; observed: 47). Please back off.", "retry_after_seconds": 18, "trace_id": "trc-ta-429-2026-05-21-09-12-04-aa"}}

Apologies, Madam — the API returned **HTTP 429 Rate Limited**: your tenant exceeded 30 list calls in 60 seconds. The server requests we back off for **18 seconds** before retrying.

- **Trace ID:** `trc-ta-429-2026-05-21-09-12-04-aa`

I will wait the indicated interval and retry. Mohon tunggu sebentar.
Aiya OK, I think my colleague just ran a bulk dashboard reload. Go ahead retry.
Retrying now after the back-off window.

| mt-arpu-prepaid-daily | ARPU Prepaid Daily | MYR |

Yes, run comparison for tariff `tp-pp-rd-3day-99` versus baseline scenario `tp-pp-rd-3day-baseline-2026q1` for the last 2 weeks. Include both ARPU weekly and topup frequency.
Running the scenario comparison now.

Comparison ready, Madam:

| Metric | W19 current | W20 current | W20 baseline | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARPU Prepaid Weekly (MYR) | 8.42 | 7.24 | 8.37 | **-13.5%** |
| Topup Frequency (per sub) | 2.81 | 2.80 | 2.82 | -0.7% |

**Insight:** Topup frequency is virtually flat, but ARPU dropped 13.5%. This means each topup is yielding less revenue — pointing to **value-per-transaction** drop, not volume drop. Could indicate a promotional discount, a customer segment mix shift, or a refund spike. Shall I run anomaly detection on the underlying data to pinpoint the cause?
Yes run anomaly detection. Use whatever dimensions are sensible — region, channel, anything that might be the cause.
Kicking off anomaly detection across region, channel, and customer segment.

Subscribe me — email kahyee.wong@myxtel.com.my. And please CC my partner Encik Tan Chong (chong.tan@myxtel.com.my), he's helping prepare the CFO slides.
Subscribing both of you to events.

While we wait, what's the closest carpark to the office? My partner is driving in for a meeting.

My apologies Madam, carpark and visitor logistics are outside the scope of the tariff analytics service. For that, please refer to **Facilities portal** at facilities.myxtel.com.my or contact the lobby reception. Returning to the analytics workflow — would you like me to prep a custom query on the underlying transaction table while we wait for the anomaly job? That way we have raw data ready to compare against the anomaly findings.
Good idea. Create a query that selects average txn value, count of refunds, and top 10 promotion codes used on tp-pp-rd-3day-99 in week W20, grouped by region. Then execute it.
Setting up the query now, then I will execute it.

Results in. Key signal stands out clearly, Madam:

| Region | Avg Txn (MYR) | Refunds | Top Promo |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Klang Valley** | **8.10** | **1,230** | PROMO-3D-NEW10 (4,500x) + WIN3D2026 (2,100x) |
| Penang | 8.45 | 210 | PROMO-3D-NEW10 |
| Johor | 8.40 | 185 | PROMO-3D-NEW10 |
| East Malaysia | 8.50 | 95 | PROMO-3D-NEW10 |
| Other Peninsular | 8.39 | 120 | PROMO-3D-NEW10 |

**Klang Valley refund count is 5-13x higher than other regions**, and the **WIN3D2026** promo only appears in KV. Strong hypothesis: a Klang Valley promotional campaign is generating excess discount + refund activity. Note the warning that the dataset is eventually consistent — last sync 09:00, so figures could shift slightly.

Shall I check the anomaly detection job to confirm it also flags this?
Yes check the job. Eh wait — actually before that, can you remind me what `PROMO-3D-NEW10` is supposed to do? I forgot which campaign that came from.

I do not have direct campaign metadata in this analytics workflow, Madam — to be fully accurate I should not guess from the code prefix alone. The dependency graph for the tariff plan should link to the originating campaign though. Let me pull that and the anomaly job in parallel.

Migrate to v2 (richer SHAP-style explanations).", "sunset_date": "2026-10-15"}}

Both results confirm the same story, Madam:

**Dependency graph:** `tp-pp-rd-3day-99` is linked to campaign `camp-prep-kv-newcomer-2026q2` (Klang Valley Newcomer 3-Day, active 10 May–10 Jun). That campaign owns both **PROMO-3D-NEW10 (10% off)** and **WIN3D2026 (25% off)** — and importantly the graph notes **stacking is being allowed in error** (ticket TKT-PROMO-201).

**Anomaly job findings:**
- Klang Valley ARPU -18.4% (anomaly score 0.91) — explained by stacked promo + refunds
- Penang -1.5% — within normal variance

**Conclusion for CFO:** the ARPU drop is **not** a market-level issue. It is a **promotion stacking bug** in the Klang Valley newcomer campaign. Recommend escalating to the promotions team to fix the stacking rule.

Additionally, a **proactive deprecation notice**: `get_anomaly_detection_job` v1 sunsets on **15 October 2026** — your platform team should plan a migration to v2.

Would you like me to generate a formal report for the CFO?
Excellent finding. Before we generate the report — can you simulate what ARPU would be **if** the stacking bug were fixed (i.e., only one promo per txn)? Just to project the recovery.
Running a what-if simulation with stacking disabled.

- **Current ARPU (KV):** MYR 7.04
- **Simulated ARPU (no stacking):** MYR 8.21
- **Recovery:** +16.6% (closes most of the gap)
- **Residual gap:** -1.9% (refunds: -1.2pp, segment mix: -0.7pp)

The simulation includes a caveat: if some refunds are themselves promo-driven, real-world recovery could exceed +16.6%. Strong message for the CFO deck. Shall I generate the formal report now?
Yes generate a PDF report titled 'Prepaid 3-Day ARPU WoW Investigation', deliver to download URL, include the findings, simulation, and dependency graph. Tag it for cfo-review.
Generating now.

Returning to the workflow — would you like to also schedule a recurring weekly report so this CFO view runs automatically each Friday?
Good idea, yes — schedule weekly Friday 8am, same report structure, deliver to my email.

Before I schedule, please confirm: this will run **every Friday at 08:00 MYT** indefinitely, pulling the rolling 7-day window automatically and emailing you the PDF. To stop it later you can call cancel. Confirm with **YES** to proceed.
YES go ahead.
Scheduling now.
